A.explanation: 43 dJ equals $4.3 \text{ J}$ which equals $4300 \text{ mJ} = 4.3 \times 10^3 \text{ mJ}$.

B.explanation: MJ means megajoule where $1 \text{ MJ} = 10^6 \text{ J}$, so this value is a million times larger than a millijoule and far larger than $4.3 \text{ J}$.

C.explanation: This is $0.0043 \text{ mJ}$, which is a million times too small because the deci to milli step was applied in the wrong direction.

D.explanation: This is $0.0043 \text{ MJ} = 4300 \text{ J}$, which is 1000 times too large due to confusing $10^{-3}$ with $10^6$.

hints: Notice the starting unit is dJ for 43 dJ and the options use mJ and MJ - recall what deci, milli and mega mean as powers of 10.
First convert 43 dJ to joules using $1 \text{ dJ} = 10^{-1} \text{ J}$, giving $4.3 \text{ J}$.
Then convert $4.3 \text{ J}$ to millijoules using $1 \text{ mJ} = 10^{-3} \text{ J}$ and check whether you must multiply or divide to get a larger number of smaller units.
walkthrough: Write the prefix values: deci $\text{d} = 10^{-1}$ and milli $\text{m} = 10^{-3}$, with mega $\text{M} = 10^6$.
Convert the given energy to the base unit joule: $43 \text{ dJ} = 43 \times 10^{-1} \text{ J} = 4.3 \text{ J}$.
Convert joules to millijoules: since $1 \text{ mJ} = 10^{-3} \text{ J}$, then $1 \text{ J} = 10^3 \text{ mJ}$.
A value in MJ would be much larger, and $10^{-3}$ would make the number smaller, so only the $10^3$ mJ form matches. This is option A.
